source: UN Resident Coordinator Namibia - Cholera Outbreak Situation Report No. 2 (as of 21 Feb 2014)
processing_notes: Source states: 'Namibia has been experiencing an outbreak of cholera since Nov 2013, previously largely confined to northern regions. The situation in particularly hard-hit Kunene was said to have been brought under control on 20 January 2014. However, additional cases with some fatalities were recorded in Kunene, as well as Otjozondjupa and Oshana regions in the last week. [UN RC Situation Report No. 2, as of 21 Feb 2014; reproduced on OCHA map 375v02 of 24 Feb 2014]' - cholera confirmed present; no case count available.

source: ReliefWeb Namibia Cholera 2013-2014 Outbreak Disaster Page
processing_notes: Source states: 'Since November 2013, Namibia has been affected by a cholera outbreak, which was initially confined to four northern regions, including hardest-hit Kunene, as well as Omusati, Oshana and Ohangwena. source: IRIN - Namibia: Cholera subsides as gastroenteritis arrives (23 January 2007)
processing_notes: Source states: 'An outbreak of cholera has killed three people in Namibia's northwestern region of Kunene, and three other people have died from dehydration caused by gastroenteritis in the same area since early December 2006 ... 'It came from Angola last October [2006], where cholera is a problem in the Cunene Province of our neighbouring country ... We only have about one case reported daily now, quite a bit down from three or four each day in November and [December]' [3 cholera deaths in Kunene; no Kunene cholera case count given]' - cholera confirmed present; no case count available.
